name: Manuel Crescencio Rejón International Airport
before:
The gateway to Yucatan, and one of the fastest growing airports in Mexico: just under 3.7 million passengers in 2024 and close to 3.94 million in 2025. That puts it ninth in the country by passenger numbers.

The location is the selling point. It sits inside the Merida urban area, less than 5 km south west of the city centre, so transfers are short in a way they are not at most Mexican gateways.

Routes run across Mexico and out to the United States, Canada, Central America and the Caribbean, with Viva treating it as a focus city. It is operated by Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste.

The site does more than scheduled passenger work. It houses the Mexican airspace navigation service and an army presence, and carries flight training and general aviation alongside the airlines. The name honours Manuel Crescencio Garcia Rejon, a jurist and politician from Yucatan.
after:
Mérida's airport, serving the city and the surrounding state of Yucatán. It handled just under 3.7 million passengers in 2024 and close to 3.94 million in 2025.

The location is the selling point. It sits less than 5 km south west of the city centre, so transfers are short.

Routes run across Mexico, and there are international flights too. It is operated by Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (ASUR). There is also a separate general aviation building.

The name honours Manuel Crescencio Rejón, a politician from Yucatán.

claims.claim: routes to the United States, Canada, Central America and the Caribbean
claims.wasBefore: out to the United States, Canada, Central America and the Caribbean
claims.why: No second source dated in the last 12 months for the regions. United States: Viva Aerobus's seasonal Los Angeles flights (to become year-round from the second half of 2026) are reported by Quadratín on 8 September 2025, just outside 12 months; Mexico News Daily's report is behind a bot check and American Airlines' newsroom refused the browser. Canada: Air Canada adds Toronto from 21 November 2026 (PAX, 7 April 2026), one source, held back below. Central America: the only story found (Guatemala City) dates from 2022. Caribbean: nothing found. Softened to 'international flights too', which ASUR's 2025 figures and Wikipedia both support.

claims.claim: Viva focus city
claims.wasBefore: with Viva treating it as a focus city
claims.why: Airline bases are time-sensitive and nothing from the last 12 months says so: the hub reports are Yucatán Magazine (31 August 2022) and Mexico Business News (Friday 9 August 2024, three aircraft based). Viva's own site is a JavaScript app that returns no text.
